messages:
eli: heads-up — noticed a recurring latency spike on prod GPUs when tool/function calls trigger mid-decode. p95 up ~40% for requests that produce structured output with stop tokens. I attached a trace snippet below. :warning:

sara: same. saw a pattern where decode batching splits when a tool pause occurs and KV cache appears to get resynced (misses) on the resumed fragment. causes kernel-selection churn. :eyes:

jing: paste from profiler (short):
```
trace: decode_start -> tool_pause (3.2ms) -> resume -> kernel_select(layer=14) -> memcpy 8.7ms -> kernel_swap 12.4ms -> kv_resync 6.1ms
metrics: batch_size_before=24, batch_size_after=6, kv_hits_before=0.98, kv_hits_after=0.42
```

jing: the kernel selection heuristic is sensitive to the observed sequence length distribution. tool pauses create fragmented sequences that look like shorter sequences, so we pick a different kernel path (quantized->fallback float) which is expensive.

ash: are we sure it’s kernel swap and not just serialization overhead during the toolcall? I pulled a flamegraph — the big chunk is memcpy + kernel swap overhead, not JS-side serialization.

devon: quick repro notes: run the decode loop with structured output prompt, inject a 50–200ms tool pause after token ~120. run with continuous batching enabled. you’ll see batch-splintering: earlier batches start evacuation, resumed requests join a small tail batch that picks the wrong kernel.

eli: I tried increasing the token_budget_target for batch formation as an experiment (default 16 -> 48). Result: fewer splits, median latency improved ~10%, but tail still bad when kv_hits drop. Suggests we need a KV prefetch/resync when toolcall is invoked.

ash: could we flag tool-invoked requests to keep KV pinned? maybe mark their KV slot as "reserved" during pauses. risk: higher memory usage + complexity in GC.

jing: alternative: when a paused request resumes, check if batch size < threshold -> force it into the previous kernel path by temporarily coercing sequence_length metadata (e.g., pretend longer) so kernel selector stays on quant path. hacky but low-cost.

devon: patch idea: in queue policy, add a short reheating window (50ms) that preferentially merges resume events back into their original batch if GPU still has that kernel loaded. heuristics: session_id affinity + last_kernel_id cache.

eli: ran bench with reheating window 50ms + hold_window bumped to 20 for toolcalls. results: p50 down 12%, p95 down 7%, but we still see rare 200ms spikes when kv_hits fall <0.5.

jing: attached a small log excerpt (sanitized):
```
[2048901201] req=A12 resume tool_pause token=128 prev_kernel=q4_2 -> selected kernel=float32_fallback
[2048901201] batch_before=18 batch_after=3 kv_hit_rate=0.38
[2048901201] memcpy=9.1ms kernel_swap=13.8ms
```

ash: bench-bot flagged a perf regression PR yesterday (https://git.company/pr/998) that changed kernel fallback threshold. Might be related. Can someone link the profiler output to that PR?

devon: I diffed the decision tree — PR lowered the seq_len threshold for q4 kernels from 96->64. Combined with tool pauses that make remaining tail <64, we flip to float32. That matches.

eli: plan proposal: (1) revert the seq_len threshold change on the kernel selection PR until we evaluate toolcall impact (2) implement reheating window + session affinity for paused/resumed requests (3) add KV-pin flag on toolcall start so we don't evict/pin default slots.

ash: +1 to revert. Quick win. Also add a profiler probe to log kernel_id at pause/resume boundaries so we can quantify how often kernel swaps happen.

jing: I'll send a small instrumented build to the canary pool with logs and reheating window toggled. expecting to see reduced kernel_swap counts.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for rev a3b9c1 (jing/reheating-window).

bench-bot: automated perf run queued. comparing baseline -> canary. expect results in ~30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

eli: thanks. if canary looks good we'll roll back the kernel-threshold change and keep reheating/kv-pin experiments behind flags. aim to close loop with concrete p95 reduction before merging.

sara: also to track: structured-output stop tokens produce uneven token distributions; add a small synthetic workload that mimics toolcall pauses for our nightly perf suite. otherwise we’ll miss regressions.

devon: noted. I’ll add a synthetic generator that emits pauses and structured outputs. should be easy to run in CI.

eli: awesome. tagging owners: jinG -> instrument + canary, devon -> synthetic workload + queue policy change, ash -> kernel-threshold revert PR, sara -> perf test integration.

bench-bot: perf results posted: canary p95 improved 9% on toolcall-heavy workload, baseline p95 still worse on mixed workloads. detailed report: https://perf.company/report/2048901234

eli: great — keep monitoring, but this looks promising. :thumbsup:

sara: follow-up: add alert if kv_hit_rate < 0.6 for >10s on a node; that should catch pathological resync conditions.

eli: good call. I'll open an alert PR.

deploy-bot: canary promoted to stable in region-us-west-2.

eli: closing thread for now — next steps captured in the ticket. thanks everyone.
